summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, asthma, and prior CABG was admitted for a three-week productive cough and one day of sharp, pleuritic chest pain. She presented with uncontrolled hyperglycemia, with blood glucose levels reaching 512 mg/dL. Evaluation revealed no evidence of pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, or acute cardiac ischemia. Chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, exacerbated by coughing. The cough improved with supportive care and was attributed to a viral upper respiratory infection. Her insulin regimen was adjusted with Lantus switched from morning to bedtime dosing, and she received education on proper insulin use. Blood glucose levels stabilized, symptoms resolved, and she was discharged home with services and follow-up arranged for diabetes and blood pressure management.
